title: Same Number, Different Groupings
objective: The same quantity can be grouped into tens and ones in more than one valid way (e.g., 34 as 3 tens 4 ones, or 2 tens 14 ones) — a direct, higher-level return of "same value, different form."
studentQuestion: Is there another way to group the same amount into tens and ones?
newIdea: Non-canonical (ungrouped/regrouped) tens-and-ones representations of the same value.

teaching.setup: 34 shown as 3 tens and 4 ones (canonical form).
teaching.see: Is 3 tens and 4 ones the only way to make 34 with tens and ones?
teaching.break: Unbundle one ten back into 10 loose ones.
teaching.build: Recount: now there are 2 tens and 14 ones — still 34.
teaching.transform: 34 as "3 tens, 4 ones" or "2 tens, 14 ones" — same value, two valid place-value forms.

check.prompt: Count all loose ones from the unbundled version — still 34.

examples.transfer: Given a non-canonical form (2 tens, 15 ones), also state the canonical form (3 tens, 5 ones).

mastery.evidence: Produces both a canonical and a regrouped form for the same two-digit number and confirms both total the same via recount.
